newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY APPROVES ASSETS RETURN ACCORD WITH VATICAN.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY APPROVES ASSETS RETURN ACCORD WITH VATICAN.

text.p: Hungary's government said it approved on Thursday a historic accord with the Vatican about returning Catholic church assets confiscated by the country's Communist regime after the Second World War.
"We have signed a historic agreement with the Holy See about financing the catholic church and meet their real estate claims," government spokesman Elemer Kiss told a news conference following.
He added that the agreement was a compromise, which "looked at both the claims and Hungary's (financial) position".

Under the accord, Hungary will return the larger part of real estates worth more than 100 billion forints by 2011, while some 42 billion forints of the total claims would be satisfied in the form of annual payments to the church, Kiss said.

Hungary also undertook that it will grant the same subsidies to educational institution kept up by the Catholic church as to schools and universities supervised by the government and local municipalities.

Probably from 1998, Hungarians will be allowed to grant one percent of their personal income tax to historic churches, and the government will complete the donations to half percent of the total personal income payments, Kiss added.
